reasoning_traces.think:
The core structure of GSE EdgeBall is defined by a dual-state system: a static draft commitment (D) and a dynamic feedback loop (L(t)). The draft sets an initial configuration that evolves under stochastic influence from what-changed feeds. Risk ladders (L(t)) model increasing uncertainty and potential outcomes, while receipts (R) provide posterior evidence for refining policy functions (π). These elements form a closed-loop system where D acts as a boundary condition, L(t) as a feedback variable, and π as a control mechanism. The failure mode occurs when feedback signals become stale or misaligned with actual performance, leading to overfitting or divergence in policy updates. The system's robustness depends on the integrity of R and the consistency of F(t), which must remain aligned with real-world outcomes.
